findings.situation: A filer has a section 179 carryover from a year before 2024 but did not file a Form 4562 for 2024, for example because the business had no depreciation or new property that year, so the carryover was never shown on a 2024 line 13.
findings.source_text: i4562 (2025) p. 5, Line 10: "The carryover of disallowed deduction from 2024 is the amount of section 179 property, if any, you elected to expense in previous years that was not allowed as a deduction because of the business income limitation. If you filed Form 4562 for 2024, enter the amount from line 13 of your 2024 Form 4562."
findings.why: The instructions define the carryover as all disallowed amounts from previous years and use the 2024 line 13 only as the source when a 2024 form was filed. The question asks only for the 2024 line 13 amount, zero if none, so this filer would answer zero and lose a carryover that line 12 needs.

findings.situation: A filer with two or more Schedules C that use the simplified home-office method has one combined 2024 carryover, and the tool adds that whole amount to each business's own 2025 elections.
findings.source_text: i4562 (2025) p. 5, Line 12: "The limitations on lines 5 and 11 apply to the taxpayer, and not to each separate business or activity... you may allocate your allowable section 179 expense deduction among them." The question asks for "The carryover of disallowed section 179 deduction from line 13 of your (and, on a joint return, your spouse's) 2024 Form 4562".
findings.why: The question collects the taxpayer's total carryover, but sc.ho_s179_max treats it as the carryover for this one business. The same carryover is then counted once for every Schedule C, which overstates each business's section 179 amount used in the simplified-method limit.

findings.situation: A filer who had more than one business in 2024 filed a "Summary" Form 4562 plus a separate Form 4562 for each business, so there are several 2024 forms with a line 13.
findings.source_text: i4562 (2025) p. 5, Line 12: "enter 'Summary' at the top of Part I of the separate Form 4562 you are completing for the total amounts from all businesses or activities... On line 12 of the Form 4562 you prepare for each separate business or activity, enter the amount allocated..."
findings.why: "line 13 of your 2024 Form 4562" could be read as the Summary form's line 13, or as one business's form, or as a sum across all the forms. These readings give different amounts, and summing could double count if the Summary form is included.
